answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, delivery continuity is the binding constraint alongside the 18% cost mandate. memory_c4 suggests renegotiating with the incumbent at renewal can recover meaningful margin without disturbing service scope, which directly serves the cost mandate while avoiding the integration/onboarding risk implied by switching vendors (memory_c2) at a moment when there's zero buffer to absorb disruption. I verified c4 and c2 specifically because they represent the two most cost-aggressive paths (renegotiate vs. switch), and the switch option carries the highest downstream delivery risk given current capacity tightness, so it needed scrutiny before being ruled out. I'm not fully closing the door on switching or adding a second source next cycle if renegotiation can't hit the 18% target, but for this single decision slot, negotiating with the incumbent is the lowest-risk lever toward the TCO objective. Confidence is moderate rather than high because I have not yet re-verified the exact terms/scope details behind c4's 'no narrowing of service scope' claim in this specific renewal window.
